question: CANON false-reject on 1M real request lines (own logs or public corpora)

corpora.cc-main-2026-43: Common Crawl Oct 2026 URL index, 989,955 URLs (913,268 distinct targets) from 1000 of 886,601 random cdx blocks, every 3rd line; crawler-normalized link URLs, many sites; benign 988,758
corpora.secrepo-2024-2026: SecRepo self.logs (www.secrepo.com, Apache combined), 2024-01-01..2026-10-22, 2,279,367 request lines; benign 1,654,694 after removing 624,673 attack/scanner lines (18,920 scanner IPs)
corpora.nasa-1995 (comparison only): NASA KSC Jul+Aug 1995 (ITA), 3,459,784 HTTP request lines; benign 3,366,062

measured.units: percent of request lines (benign-only), any-hit per clause; sole-cause in parentheses; decision uses max over the two 2024-2026 sources
measured.hardware: this laptop, python 3.12 stdlib, canon_ref.py imported unmodified; detector-vs-reference reject/accept disagreements = 0 on all 10.4M lines

p.raw_nonascii.decision: keep reject (secrepo hits are mostly GBK backup-archive probes the heuristic misses)

p.trailing_slash (already 308 in canon_r.decision: FLIP the 308: trailing slash is a distinct single reading, accept

measured.cc_pct_nonascii_paths: 28,223 paths with %80-%FF: 1 invalid UTF-8, 190 valid but not NFC (0.019% of all lines)

semantics of the added values.encoded_non_ascii_path=accept_opaque: %80-%FF escapes in a path are kept as uppercase-hex octets, never decoded or Unicode-normalized for matching (RFC 3986 6.2.2.1 only); still reject if the octets are not strict UTF-8 (overlong, surrogates) or not NFC (0.019% of CC lines). Enum: reject | accept_opaque.
semantics of the added values.empty_segments=redirect_308: '//' inside a path answers 308 to the slash-merged path; nothing is forwarded in the non-canonical form. Enum: reject | redirect_308.
semantics of the added values.trailing_slash=accept: '/a/' is its own canonical form (distinct from '/a'), as RFC 3986 defines; the canon_ref '308 strip' rule would redirect 40% of CC URLs and would loop on sites whose own canonical form is '/a/' (e.g. WordPress redirect_canonical; known behaviour, not measured here). Enum: accept | redirect_308_strip.
semantics of the added values.query=opaque: the query is canonicalized only by 6.2.2.1/6.2.2.2 and otherwise forwarded byte-exact; AEGIS never splits it, and authz never keys on it (CANON-5). Still rejected in opaque mode: bad percent-escape, raw non-ASCII, raw space/forbidden ASCII, encoded or raw NUL/controls, '#', length > 8192, '&&' empty pair, empty name, %2B. A route that declares typed parameters gets query=strict for that route (the current canon_query rules, with declared list parameters exempt from dup_name). Enum: strict | opaque.

decision_effect.unchanged: all other CANON-2 path rejects (encoded / \ ; NUL ctrl %25, raw \ ;, dot segments, raw non-ASCII), host rules and header rules

rung: measurement grade B (public real-world corpora, not AEGIS traffic; one small site plus a crawler-derived URL sample; laptop run)
reproduce: DL=$DL spikes/q4-008/run.sh   # every step via ci/heavy.sh; writes spikes/q4-008/results/{*.json,summary.json,table.md,cc_utf8_check.txt}
limits: Era/site bias: SecRepo is one static security-dataset site with Apache autoindex (its own '?C=M;O=A' sort links drive q.semicolon/q.multi_eq) and heavy scanner load; CC URLs are link-derived and crawler-normalized (dot segments resolved, raw non-ASCII percent-encoded, hosts as A-labels), so CC under-counts dot_segment, raw_nonascii and non_ascii_host and is not a browser request stream; NASA 1995 is pre-modern (imagemap/isindex queries) and never decides. No API, mobile-app, gRPC-gateway or SPA traffic, no Host header in the access logs (host clauses measured on CC authorities only). The benign heuristic is signature-based and misses some probes (ThinkPHP invokefunction, GBK backup-archive names), which inflates benign rates slightly; it never decided a verdict. Encoded slash (0.048% CC, click-tracker paths) is the reject clause closest to the threshold after p.semicolon (0.086%).
